findings.reason: the section's premise and its base-arm measure are both unfalsified-but-unreproduced as written, so a dispatched node would set out to halve a probe that already answers at a third of the bound, and its declared base arm would fail for a reason that is not a defect in the code.
findings.text: §40's Why asserts the probe "has grown to the bound" and that a loadable checkout "reads as one that 'does not import' whenever the node is busy", and its done-when requires "five fresh runs of the probe on the fleet node" with "the base median … over" the 15 s head target; measured here, on the node the Why names (98dci4-clu-2002, load average 29.3 on 8 CPUs, 2026-10-17T03:19–03:22Z), the production probe (`reckon.crew_follow_commands._FOLLOWER_RELOAD_PROBE` run exactly as `checkout_trust.reckon_imports` runs it, against the main checkout) took thirteen samples over three windows bounded by 6.8 s and 11.1 s with median ≈9 s against the 30.0 s bound — every one of them at or under a third of the bound, so the base arm the done-when demands is not reproducible; separately, the Why's own timeline does not support the causal claim that the deferred reload stalled the snapshots, since the staleness it cites runs from 02:57:48Z, before the ~03:03Z merge (773e7e542, 2026-10-17 03:01:57Z) it blames

findings.reason: the one precedent offered for the "import less" route was deliberately retired three days before §40 was written, and it is the partial probe whose divergence from the follower's full probe the unification replaced, so a node reading this anchor either searches for it in vain or re-adopts the design that was just removed.
findings.text: the deliverable's first route ("it imports less … as `mcp._CODE_IMPORT_PROBE` imports only `reckon.mcp`") names a symbol that does not exist: a repository-wide search finds it only in prose, and `docs/evidence/archive/an-mcp-failure-names-its-cause-landed.html` records that the landed `an-mcp-failure-names-its-cause` §14 removed it ("the follower's reloader and `_stale_code_response` in `reckon/mcp.py` both call it, and `_CODE_IMPORT_PROBE` is gone", merge `096844cd8`, 2026-10-14)

findings.reason: half the deliverable is unmeasured, so a node that changes only the message satisfies every declared case while leaving the timeout retried only on the next stomp move.
findings.text: §40's deliverable requires that a timed-out probe "is reported as a timeout, not as an image that does not import, **and it is retried at the next poll**", but the done-when's only test covers the reported wording; the current code sets `self.deferred_stamp = current_stamp` on the not-reloadable branch (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:354`), and `poll` then returns early on `current_stamp == self.deferred_stamp` (:333), so today a deferral is retried only "when the code changes" — the echo's own words (:358) — and the poll-cadence retry is a behaviour change the done-when never exercises

findings.reason: the conventional id a later node or outcome would form (`f-tmstwiw-040`) matches no element, so the followup cannot be resolved by the naming convention every sibling follows and risks being left open beside a landed §40.
findings.text: the new open followup carries `data-id="f-tmswiw-040"` while all thirteen other followups on this plan use the abbreviation its slug yields (`f-tmstwiw-001`, `-close`, `-031-033`, `-037`, `-039`, …), so §40's routing address is off-scheme by one character

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §40's deliverable cites `mcp._CODE_IMPORT_PROBE` as the precedent for importing less, but that symbol was deleted on 2026-10-14 and resolves nowhere in the repository.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §40's done-when tests only the wording of the deferral line, while the deliverable also requires a timed-out probe to be *retried at the next poll*, which nothing measures.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the timing report and every control are written "under the run directory", which is durable, and the new test lives in `tests/`; no session-scratchpad path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §40 and its new test name the mechanism (`_FOLLOWER_RELOAD_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `tests/test_a_reload_probe_timeout_is_not_a_broken_image.py`); no plan label, phase name or ticket number reaches code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §40's root cause ("The package has grown to the bound", "a loadable checkout reads as one that 'does not import' whenever the node is busy") is not reproduced: the production probe runs in a third of its bound on the named node under load, and the timeline does not connect the deferred reload to the stale snapshot it blames.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §40 names one goal (the reload proof stops misreading a loadable checkout and answers inside its bound); its message and retry clauses are properties of that one proof, not a second deliverable.
